newsitem.title: UK: M&S hits peak amid ebullient stores sector.
newsitem.headline: M&S hits peak amid ebullient stores sector.

text.p: Marks and Spencer Plc hit an all-time high on Friday amid buoyant retail stocks, with dealers and analysts attributing the gains to a number of bullish factors.
M&S put on 10p to 530p by 1215 GMT after briefly touching an record intraday peak of 537 earlier in the session. Trading volume in the shares, which rose 9p on Thursday, was more than seven million.

Analysts and dealers said the sector has underperformed a strongly rising market and was catching up. In addition, good figures from the British Retail Consortium (BRC) on Tuesday continued to provide support, they said.
The BRC said UK retail sales grew by 4.8 percent year-on-year in May compared with an upwardly revised April growth rate of 4.1 percent.

"Marks is seeing good volume and is squeezing higher so there's obviously a good buyer around. It's got a bit of catching up to do but there's no concrete story in Marks or the rest of the sector," one dealer said.
GUS Plc rose 19p to 681-1/2p and Next Plc 5-1/2p to 746-1/2p.
Argos Plc rose 8-1/2p to 587-1/2p and Dixons Group Plc 9p to 517-1/2p on hopes of a spending boom from consumers' windfall gains from building society flotations, analysts said.

Analysts said news that The John Lewis Partnership's department store sales rose 11.8 percent last week from the same week last year was not an influence. In the 19 weeks to June 7, sales were up 9.3 percent.
